audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Macedonia/Greece, Eutychus, Troas bread-breaking, travel itinerary, Miletus farewell, serving with tears, Spirit-bound Jerusalem, guarding flock, no coveting, blessed to give.

verses.restored: After the uproar ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, encouraged them, said farewell, and departed to go to Macedonia.

familiar.text: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia.

modern.text: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.

original.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ παύσασθαι τὸν θόρυβον ⸀μεταπεμψάμενος ὁ Παῦλος τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ ⸀παρακαλέσας, ἀσπασάμενος ἐξῆλθεν ⸀πορεύεσθαι ⸀εἰς Μακεδονίαν.

verses.restored: Passing through those regions and encouraging them with many words, he came to Greece.

familiar.text: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,

modern.text: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement, he arrived in Greece,

original.text: διελθὼν δὲ τὰ μέρη ἐκεῖνα καὶ παρακαλέσας αὐτοὺς λόγῳ πολλῷ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα

verses.restored: After spending three months, when a plot was made against him by the Judeans as he was about to sail to Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.

familiar.text: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.

modern.text: where he stayed three months. And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.

original.text: ποιήσας τε μῆνας τρεῖς· γενομένης ⸂ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῷ⸃ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων μέλλοντι ἀνάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν Συρίαν ἐγένετο ⸀γνώμης τοῦ ὑποστρέφειν διὰ Μακεδονίας.

verses.restored: Sopater of Berea, son of Pyrrhus, accompanied him; also Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia.

familiar.text: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.

modern.text: Paul was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.

original.text: συνείπετο δὲ ⸀αὐτῷ Σώπατρος ⸀Πύρρου Βεροιαῖος, Θεσσαλονικέων δὲ Ἀρίσταρχος καὶ Σεκοῦνδος, καὶ Γάϊος Δερβαῖος καὶ Τιμόθεος, Ἀσιανοὶ δὲ Τυχικὸς καὶ Τρόφιμος·

verses.restored: These went ahead and were waiting for us in Troas.

familiar.text: These going before tarried for us at Troas.

modern.text: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.

original.text: οὗτοι ⸀δὲ ⸀προσελθόντες ἔμενον ἡμᾶς ἐν Τρῳάδι·

verses.restored: But we sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and in five days came to them at Troas, where we spent seven days.

familiar.text: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.

modern.text: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi, and five days later we rejoined them in Troas, where we stayed seven days. Eutychus Revived at Troas (2 Kings 4:18–37)

original.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐξεπλεύσαμεν μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας τῶν ἀζύμων ἀπὸ Φιλίππων, καὶ ἤλθομεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα ἄχρι ἡμερῶν πέντε, ⸀οὗ διετρίψαμεν ἡμέρας ἑπτά.

verses.restored: On the first day of the week, when we were gathered to break bread, Paul was reasoning with them, intending to depart the next day; he extended the word until midnight.

familiar.text: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.

modern.text: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread. Since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight.

original.text: Ἐν δὲ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων συνηγμένων ⸀ἡμῶν κλάσαι ἄρτον ὁ Παῦλος διελέγετο αὐτοῖς, μέλλων ἐξιέναι τῇ ἐπαύριον, παρέτεινέν τε τὸν λόγον μέχρι μεσονυκτίου.

verses.restored: There were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.

familiar.text: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.

modern.text: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.

original.text: ἦσαν δὲ λαμπάδες ἱκαναὶ ἐν τῷ ὑπερῴῳ οὗ ἦμεν συνηγμένοι·

verses.restored: A certain young man named Eutychus, sitting at the window, being overcome by deep sleep as Paul reasoned at length, was carried down by sleep and fell from the third story, and was taken up dead.

familiar.text: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.

modern.text: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.

original.text: ⸀καθεζόμενος δέ τις νεανίας ὀνόματι Εὔτυχος ἐπὶ τῆς θυρίδος, καταφερόμενος ὕπνῳ βαθεῖ διαλεγομένου τοῦ Παύλου ἐπὶ πλεῖον, κατενεχθεὶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἔπεσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ τριστέγου κάτω καὶ ἤρθη νεκρός.

verses.restored: Paul went down, fell upon him, and embracing him said, Do not be troubled, for his life/soul is in him.

familiar.text: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.

modern.text: But Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. “Do not be alarmed!” he said. “He is still alive!”

original.text: καταβὰς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐπέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ συμπεριλαβὼν εἶπεν· Μὴ θορυβεῖσθε, ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐστιν.

verses.restored: Going up, breaking the bread and eating, he conversed for a long while until daybreak, and so departed.

familiar.text: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.

modern.text: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak, he departed.

original.text: ἀναβὰς δὲ καὶ κλάσας ⸀τὸν ἄρτον καὶ γευσάμενος ἐφʼ ἱκανόν τε ὁμιλήσας ἄχρι αὐγῆς, οὕτως ἐξῆλθεν.

verses.restored: They brought the child alive and were comforted not moderately.

familiar.text: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.

modern.text: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive. From Troas to Miletus

original.text: ἤγαγον δὲ τὸν παῖδα ζῶντα, καὶ παρεκλήθησαν οὐ μετρίως.

verses.restored: We went ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, intending there to take Paul aboard, for so he had arranged, intending himself to go by land.

familiar.text: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.

modern.text: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.

original.text: Ἡμεῖς δὲ ⸀προελθόντες ⸀ἐπὶ τὸ πλοῖον ἀνήχθημεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἆσσον, ἐκεῖθεν μέλλοντες ἀναλαμβάνειν τὸν Παῦλον, οὕτως γὰρ ⸂διατεταγμένος ἦν⸃ μέλλων αὐτὸς πεζεύειν.

verses.restored: When he met us at Assos, taking him aboard, we came to Mitylene.

familiar.text: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.

modern.text: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.

original.text: ὡς δὲ ⸀συνέβαλλεν ἡμῖν εἰς τὴν Ἆσσον, ἀναλαβόντες αὐτὸν ἤλθομεν εἰς Μιτυλήνην,

verses.restored: Sailing from there, the next day we arrived opposite Chios; the next day we touched at Samos, and the day after we came to Miletus.

familiar.text: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.

modern.text: Sailing on from there, we arrived the next day opposite Chios. The day after that we arrived at Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.

original.text: κἀκεῖθεν ἀποπλεύσαντες τῇ ἐπιούσῃ κατηντήσαμεν ⸀ἄντικρυς Χίου, τῇ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ παρεβάλομεν εἰς ⸀Σάμον, τῇ ⸀δὲ ἐχομένῃ ἤλθομεν εἰς Μίλητον·

verses.restored: For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he might not spend time in Asia; for he was hurrying, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem for the day of Pentecost.

familiar.text: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.

modern.text: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid spending time in the province of Asia, because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost. Paul’s Farewell to the Ephesians

original.text: ⸀κεκρίκει γὰρ ὁ Παῦλος παραπλεῦσαι τὴν Ἔφεσον, ὅπως μὴ γένηται αὐτῷ χρονοτριβῆσαι ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ἔσπευδεν γὰρ εἰ δυνατὸν ⸀εἴη αὐτῷ τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς γενέσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

verses.restored: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called the elders of the assembly.

familiar.text: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.

modern.text: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.

original.text: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς Μιλήτου πέμψας εἰς Ἔφεσον μετεκαλέσατο τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας.

verses.restored: When they came to him, he said to them, You yourselves know from the first day I set foot in Asia how I was with you the whole time,

familiar.text: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,

modern.text: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.

original.text: ὡς δὲ παρεγένοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ἀπὸ πρώτης ἡμέρας ἀφʼ ἧς ἐπέβην εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν πῶς μεθʼ ὑμῶν τὸν πάντα χρόνον ἐγενόμην,

verses.restored: serving the Lord with all humility and tears and trials that happened to me by the plots of the Judeans,

familiar.text: Serving the LORD with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:

modern.text: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.

original.text: δουλεύων τῷ κυρίῳ μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης ⸀καὶ δακρύων καὶ πειρασμῶν τῶν συμβάντων μοι ἐν ταῖς ἐπιβουλαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων·

verses.restored: how I held back nothing of what was profitable, not failing to announce to you and teach you publicly and house by house,

familiar.text: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,

modern.text: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,

original.text: ὡς οὐδὲν ὑπεστειλάμην τῶν συμφερόντων τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι ὑμῖν καὶ διδάξαι ὑμᾶς δημοσίᾳ καὶ κατʼ οἴκους,

verses.restored: testifying both to Judeans and Greeks of turning/realignment toward the Divine and trust toward our Lord Jesus.

familiar.text: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.

modern.text: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.

original.text: διαμαρτυρόμενος Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τὴν ⸀εἰς θεὸν μετάνοιαν καὶ ⸀πίστιν εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ⸀Ἰησοῦν.

verses.restored: And now, look, bound in the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that will meet me there,

familiar.text: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:

modern.text: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.

original.text: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ⸂δεδεμένος ἐγὼ⸃ τῷ πνεύματι πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ συναντήσοντά ⸀μοι μὴ εἰδώς,

verses.restored: except that the holy Spirit testifies to me city by city, saying that bonds and pressures await me.

familiar.text: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

modern.text: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.

original.text: πλὴν ὅτι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατὰ πόλιν διαμαρτύρεταί ⸀μοι λέγον ὅτι δεσμὰ ⸂καὶ θλίψεις με⸃ μένουσιν·

verses.restored: But I make my life/soul of no account to myself as precious, if only I may complete my course and the service that I received from the Lord Jesus: to bear witness to the good news of the grace of the Divine.

familiar.text: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.

modern.text: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.

original.text: ἀλλʼ οὐδενὸς ⸀λόγου ⸀ποιοῦμαι τὴν ⸀ψυχὴν τιμίαν ἐμαυτῷ ὡς ⸀τελειῶσαι τὸν δρόμον ⸀μου καὶ τὴν διακονίαν ἣν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, διαμαρτύρασθαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: And now, look, I know that all of you among whom I went about proclaiming the reign will see my face no more.

familiar.text: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.

modern.text: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.

original.text: Καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι οὐκέτι ὄψεσθε τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ὑμεῖς πάντες ἐν οἷς διῆλθον κηρύσσων τὴν ⸀βασιλείαν.

verses.restored: Therefore I testify to you in this day that I am clean from the blood of all,

familiar.text: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.

modern.text: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men.

original.text: ⸀διότι μαρτύρομαι ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σήμερον ἡμέρᾳ ὅτι καθαρός ⸀εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος πάντων,

verses.restored: for I did not hold back from announcing to you the whole counsel of the Divine.

familiar.text: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.

modern.text: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God.

original.text: οὐ γὰρ ὑπεστειλάμην τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι ⸂πᾶσαν τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῖν⸃.

verses.restored: Pay attention to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the holy Spirit set you as overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Divine, which he acquired through his own blood.

familiar.text: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.

modern.text: Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.

original.text: ⸀προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς καὶ παντὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ, ἐν ᾧ ὑμᾶς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔθετο ἐπισκόπους, ποιμαίνειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ, ἣν περιεποιήσατο διὰ τοῦ ⸂αἵματος τοῦ ἰδίου⸃.

verses.restored: I know that after my departure, heavy wolves will enter among you, not sparing the flock.

familiar.text: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

modern.text: I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.

original.text: ἐγὼ ⸀οἶδα ὅτι εἰσελεύσονται μετὰ τὴν ἄφιξίν μου λύκοι βαρεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς μὴ φειδόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου,

verses.restored: And from among your own selves men will arise speaking twisted things, to draw away the disciples after them.

familiar.text: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.

modern.text: Even from your own number, men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.

original.text: καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ἀναστήσονται ἄνδρες λαλοῦντες διεστραμμένα τοῦ ἀποσπᾶν τοὺς μαθητὰς ὀπίσω ⸀ἑαυτῶν·

verses.restored: Therefore stay awake, remembering that for three years, night and day, I did not cease admonishing each one with tears.

familiar.text: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.

modern.text: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.

original.text: διὸ γρηγορεῖτε, μνημονεύοντες ὅτι τριετίαν νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν οὐκ ἐπαυσάμην μετὰ δακρύων νουθετῶν ἕνα ἕκαστον.

verses.restored: And now I entrust you to the Divine and to the word of his grace, which is able to build and to give the inheritance among all those sanctified.

familiar.text: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.

modern.text: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.

original.text: καὶ τὰ νῦν παρατίθεμαι ⸀ὑμᾶς τῷ ⸀θεῷ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, τῷ δυναμένῳ ⸀οἰκοδομῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι ⸀τὴν κληρονομίαν ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πᾶσιν.

verses.restored: I coveted no one's silver or gold or clothing.

familiar.text: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.

modern.text: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.

original.text: ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα·

verses.restored: You yourselves know that these hands served my needs and those with me.

familiar.text: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.

modern.text: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.

original.text: αὐτοὶ γινώσκετε ὅτι ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσι μετʼ ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται.

verses.restored: In all things I showed you that by laboring thus it is necessary to help the weak and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

familiar.text: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

modern.text: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

original.text: πάντα ὑπέδειξα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως κοπιῶντας δεῖ ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι τῶν ἀσθενούντων, μνημονεύειν τε τῶν λόγων τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ ὅτι αὐτὸς εἶπεν Μακάριόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον διδόναι ἢ λαμβάνειν.

verses.restored: Saying these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.

familiar.text: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.

modern.text: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.

original.text: Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν θεὶς τὰ γόνατα αὐτοῦ σὺν πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς προσηύξατο.

verses.restored: There was considerable weeping by all, and falling upon Paul's neck, they were kissing him,

familiar.text: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,

modern.text: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.

original.text: ἱκανὸς δὲ ⸂κλαυθμὸς ἐγένετο⸃ πάντων, καὶ ἐπιπεσόντες ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ Παύλου κατεφίλουν αὐτόν,

verses.restored: especially grieving over the word he had spoken, that they were about to behold his face no more. They escorted him to the ship.

familiar.text: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.

modern.text: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.

original.text: ὀδυνώμενοι μάλιστα ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ᾧ εἰρήκει ὅτι οὐκέτι μέλλουσιν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ θεωρεῖν. προέπεμπον δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον.
